# 8. Mechanisms to prevent adverse consequences to the complainant in discrimination and harassment cases. 

JSL has implemented a robust mechanism and defined procedures to ensure protection against any adverse consequences for complainants in cases of discrimination and harassment. The Company upholds the dignity, privacy, and personal rights of every employee and is committed to maintaining a workplace that is free from discrimination and harassment. In this regard, the Company has established a Diversity, Equity and Inclusivity (DEI) Policy that promotes inclusiveness and equal employment opportunities for all employees, irrespective of gender, race, religion, caste, ethnic origin, nationality, age, or any other status protected under applicable laws and regulations in the Company’s operating locations. Further, under the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Policy and Whistle-blower Mechanism, JSL is committed to safeguarding the identity of complainants and ensuring strict confidentiality in handling all such matters. Under the POSH framework, aggrieved individuals may submit complaints of sexual harassment to the Chairperson or any member of the Internal Committee (IC) in writing. All complaints are handled with the highest level of confidentiality by IC members. The IC conducts a comprehensive investigation process, which includes interactions with the aggrieved party, review of evidence, examination of witnesses, and consultation with relevant experts, prior to preparing its findings and recommending appropriate action. The Company also ensures that no employee or stakeholder involved in the process is subjected to victimization or any form of adverse treatment. In addition, regular awareness and training sessions are conducted to ensure employees and stakeholders are well-informed about sexual harassment prevention and the available grievance redressal mechanisms. The Company’s Whistle-blower Policy can be accessed at: <u>https://www.jindalstainless.com/corporategovernance/policies/</u> 

9. Do human rights requirements form part of your business agreements and contracts? (Yes/No) 

Yes, as part of its contractual framework, business agreements with value chain partners, as applicable, mandate strict compliance with all relevant statutory laws, regulations, and rules enacted thereunder. This ensures that all partners operate in alignment with applicable legal and regulatory requirements. In addition, JSL has established a comprehensive Supplier Code of Conduct that sets clear expectations for ethical, responsible, and lawful business practices across the supply chain. The Code provides extensive coverage of human rights and labour-related principles, reinforcing the Company’s commitment to responsible sourcing and sustainable supply chain management. Key areas addressed under the Supplier Code of Conduct include prohibition of child labour and forced or compulsory labour, respect for freedom of association and collective bargaining, and strict adherence to non-discrimination and fair disciplinary practices. It also outlines requirements related to occupational health and safety, working hours, compensation and wage practices, security practices, as well as broader expectations on supply chain integrity and robust management systems. Through these measures, JSL ensures that its value chain partners uphold the same ethical standards and human rights principles that the Company follows, thereby promoting responsible business conduct across its entire ecosystem.

10.  Briefly describe the waste management practices adopted in your establishments. Describe the strategy adopted by your company to reduce usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products and processes and the practices adopted to manage such wastes 

The Company has established a comprehensive and integrated waste management framework anchored in the principles of Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, and Recover. This approach is closely aligned with its broader sustainability agenda, focusing on minimizing the use of hazardous and toxic substances across products and processes while maximizing resource efficiency and circularity. Key elements of the waste management strategy include: 

- Recycling and Material Recovery: Stainless steel production is significantly driven by the use of recycled scrap and recovery of metals from slag and grinding dust, thereby reducing reliance on virgin raw materials. An on-site metal recovery facility further enhances circularity by efficiently extracting valuable metals from slag and effluent treatment plant (ETP) sludge. 

- Fly Ash and By-product Utilization: Fly ash generated from the Captive Power Plant is fully utilized by cement manufacturers, brick producers, and in infrastructure projects such as road construction by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). Other by-products, including mill scale from Cold Rolling Mills and bag filter dust from the steel Melting Shop, are effectively reused in ferro-alloy production. 

- Hazardous Waste Management: The Company ensures stringent monitoring, handling, and disposal of hazardous waste in compliance with regulatory requirements. Used oil, waste oil, and e-waste are channelled to authorized recyclers registered with the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) and Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). Additionally, ETP sludge from the Cold Rolling Mill is partially repurposed for briquette manufacturing, with the balance disposed of through authorized common hazardous waste treatment facilities. 

- Plastic and Bio-Medical Waste Management: All plastic waste is routed to authorized recyclers, with vendors compliant under the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework of CPCB. Bio-medical waste is managed through certified common biomedical waste treatment facilities, ensuring safe and compliant disposal. 

- Waste Segregation and Responsible Disposal: Waste is systematically collected, segregated, and stored by category before being transferred to authorized vendors for recycling, recovery, or safe disposal. This includes hazardous streams such as used oil and bag house filter dust, which are further processed at briquette plants.

- 3 Implementation of Trickle Fills in Cooling Towers to Improve Heat Transfer Efficiency and Reduce Choking. 

Captive Power Plant Cooling Tower Efficiency Improvement Initiative: 

To strengthen energy efficiency in thermal power operations, trickle fills were implemented in cooling towers to mitigate choking, improve heat transfer stability, and enhance condenser performance. This intervention resulted in improved cooling effectiveness, reduced auxiliary power demand, and a measurable turbine heat rate improvement contributing to overall fuel savings and operational sustainability. 

The initiative led to improved cooling tower effectiveness and condenser performance, resulting in a heat rate reduction of approximately 12 kcal/kWh, lower fuel consumption, reduced auxiliary power requirement, and corresponding avoidance of greenhouse gas emissions.

5. Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100 words/ web link. 

JSL has implemented a robust and comprehensive Onsite Emergency Plan and Disaster Management framework to ensure resilience and uninterrupted business operations in the face of potential disruptions, including fires, explosions, cyber incidents, and other critical emergencies. This framework underscores the Company’s strong commitment to operational continuity, risk mitigation, and stakeholder safety. The strategy has been developed through rigorous benchmarking against industry best practices and global standards in Business Continuity Management, ensuring alignment with leading approaches to emergency preparedness and response. 

At its core, the framework is supported by a clearly defined governance structure with well-articulated roles and responsibilities, enabling swift decision-making and effective coordination during crisis situations. 

This structured and proactive approach ensures a timely, organized, and efficient response to emergencies, with a primary focus on safeguarding employees, minimizing operational disruptions, and maintaining the continuity of critical business functions.

6. Disclose any significant adverse impact to the environment, arising from the value chain of the entity. What mitigation or adaptation measures have been taken by the entity in this regard. 

JSL recognizes the pivotal role its value chain partners play in advancing its environmental and broader sustainability objectives. While no material adverse environmental impacts have been identified across the value chain, the Company maintains a proactive and vigilant approach to monitoring potential risks related to sourcing, logistics, and thirdparty operations. 

To effectively manage and mitigate environmental impacts across its value chain, JSL has instituted a structured and comprehensive framework, including: 

- Robust Policy Framework: Implementation of a Group-level Supplier Code of Conduct and Responsible Sourcing Policy, clearly articulating expectations on environmental compliance, resource efficiency, emissions management, and waste reduction for all suppliers and contractors. 

- Active Supplier Engagement: Continuous collaboration with value chain partners to promote sustainable practices, share environmental performance benchmarks, and provide guidance on reducing carbon emissions, enhancing waste management, and adopting cleaner, more efficient technologies. 

- Responsible Partnership Approach: Development of long-term, trust-based relationships anchored in transparency, accountability, and a shared commitment to environmental stewardship. 

By embedding sustainability principles into supplier engagement and decision-making, JSL aims to drive meaningful environmental improvements across its value chain, foster responsible business practices, and create long-term shared value for all stakeholders.

# Remarks: 

Suppliers are integral to the Company’s operational excellence and sustainability journey. Demonstrating a strong commitment to ethical sourcing and responsible supply chain management, JSL has instituted a comprehensive Supplier Code of Conduct and Responsible Sourcing Policy. These frameworks clearly define expectations across key areas, including environmental stewardship, social responsibility, health and safety practices, fair working conditions, ethical business conduct, and compliance with all applicable laws and regulations. In line with JSL’s Supplier Code of Conduct, all suppliers are required to adhere to relevant statutory and regulatory requirements. As a mandatory prerequisite for onboarding and engagement, suppliers must formally acknowledge their commitment by signing and stamping the Code of Conduct prior to entering into any business transaction. Additionally, the supplier evaluation process incorporates key sustainability parameters, including ISO 45001 certification, ensuring alignment with globally recognized occupational health and safety standards.

## 3. Describe the mechanisms to receive and redress grievances of the community 

Regular and continuous dialogue with communities has enabled JSL to design and implement initiatives that effectively address localized social challenges. The Company has further strengthened its engagement through CSR programmes delivered both independently and in collaboration with NGOs across its plant locations. These initiatives are co-created with key community stakeholders—including women, farmers, youth, schools, government representatives, and local panchayats—ensuring an inclusive, participatory, and need-based approach. 

JSL’s interventions are focused on driving meaningful social impact through women empowerment and livelihood generation, delivery of healthcare services in remote areas, skill development for youth, and improving access to safe drinking water in schools. 

To complement its engagement efforts, JSL has instituted a robust Stakeholder Grievance Redressal Policy with a welldefined, step-by-step mechanism. This includes timely receipt and acknowledgement of grievances, detailed assessment and investigation, structured resolution, clear communication of outcomes to the complainant, and formal closure. This framework ensures transparency, accountability, and effective resolution of community concerns.

# PRINCIPLE 9 

# Businesses should engage with and provide value to their consumers in a responsible manner 

“We adopt a customer-centric and responsible approach to delivering value, supported by structured grievance mechanisms and transparent communication systems. The Company ensures 100% disclosure of product safety information through Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) and maintains zero instances of data breaches. Through robust quality assurance processes and continuous customer engagement, JSL reinforces product safety, transparency, and trust across its customer base.” 

# Essential Indicators 

1. Describe the mechanisms in place to receive and respond to consumer complaints and feedback. 

JSL follows a customer-centric approach aimed at enhancing overall customer experience through a structured and technology-enabled customer management system catering to both domestic and export markets. This system enables customers to seamlessly lodge complaints and receive timely, transparent responses. 

For domestic customers, complaints are registered through the Hybris platform/C4C portal, while export-related concerns are logged by the Sales team in SAP, along with all necessary supporting documentation. Each complaint is assigned a unique identification code, triggering an automated workflow that promptly notifies all relevant stakeholders.

A central technical quality team reviews each case, seeking additional inputs from customers where required. Depending on the nature and complexity of the issue, site visits may be conducted by JSL’s technical experts, and product samples may be collected for detailed analysis. An interim acknowledgement is shared within 24 hours by the Quality Assurance team, followed by a comprehensive technical settlement note based on the findings. 

Customers are encouraged to review the proposed resolution and share their feedback. In cases where the resolution is not accepted, the matter is escalated to senior leadership, including the Head – Central Quality, for final closure. All complaints are resolved in line with mutually agreed Service Level Agreements (SLAs), with technical closure targeted within 30 days of complaint registration for export cases. 

This structured and responsive mechanism ensures timely resolution, accountability, and continuous improvement in customer satisfaction.

The policy incorporates key controls such as access management, data protection protocols, incident response mechanisms, and regular monitoring to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The policy can be accessed here: https://www.jindalstainless.com/ <u>wp-content/uploads/2025/02/JSL-Information-Security-Policy.pdf</u>

This integrated approach reflects the Company’s commitment to maintaining robust information security practices and strengthening resilience against cyber threats.

2. Steps taken to inform and educate consumers about safe and responsible usage of products and/or services 

JSL actively engages with its diverse customer segments to build awareness around the technical attributes, applications, and responsible usage of its products. 

To ensure ease of access and transparency, comprehensive product-related information is publicly available through the Company’s product brochure (Stainless Steel Product Brochure - Jindal Stainless), enabling stakeholders to make informed decisions. 

Beyond digital resources, JSL strengthens customer engagement through regular cross-functional visits to customer locations. These interactions facilitate a deeper understanding of customer requirements and enable detailed technical discussions to ensure optimal product selection and application. 

The Company also conducts structured annual training sessions led by its sales and technical teams, aimed at educating customers and end-users on the benefits, performance characteristics, and safe usage of stainless steel. In addition, JSL organizes dedicated fabricator training programmes, equipping participants with practical knowledge and technical expertise to enhance product application and quality outcomes. 

To further expand outreach and on-ground engagement, JSL deploys company-owned display vans for conducting customer training programmes and actively participates in industry expos and exhibitions. These initiatives collectively strengthen awareness, promote best practices, and reinforce the safe and efficient use of stainless steel across the value chain. 

3. Mechanisms in place to inform consumers of any risk of disruption/discontinuation of essential services 

Customers are proactively informed of any potential disruption or discontinuation of essential services through direct communication channels, including emails and outreach by Key Account Managers. 

In the event of significant disruptions impacting product supply, the Company ensures broader stakeholder communication through official channels such as its website, social media platforms, and press releases. This structured approach enables timely, transparent, and consistent dissemination of information to customers and other stakeholders. 

4. Does the entity display product information on the product over and above what is mandated as per local laws? (Yes/No/Not Applicable) If yes, provide details in brief. Did your entity carry out any survey with regard to consumer satisfaction relating to the major products / services of the entity, significant locations of operation of the entity or the entity as a whole? (Yes/No) 

Yes, JSL maintains a high standard of product transparency and regulatory compliance through a robust and standardized labelling system. Each product is clearly marked with critical details, including product grade, batch number, heat number, dimensions, quantity, and relevant certification logos, in alignment with REACH and RoHS requirements for 200, 300, and 400 series stainless steel grades. 

Further strengthening its compliance framework, the Company adheres to multiple Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) certifications, with ISI marks incorporated across applicable product categories. These include certifications under key standards such as IS 5522:2014, IS 15997:2012, IS 6911:2017, IS 9294:1979, IS 9516:1980, and IS 14650:2023, covering a wide range of stainless-steel applications from utensils and appliances to industrial and re-rolling products. 

This comprehensive approach ensures not only regulatory adherence but also enhances product traceability, quality assurance, and customer confidence, reinforcing JSL’s position as a reliable and compliant stainless-steel manufacturer.

## **Independent Assurance Statement to Jindal Stainless Limited on its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting for FY 2025-26** 

### **The Board of Directors,**

### **Nature of Assurance** 

SGS India Private Limited (hereinafter referred to as ‘SGS India’) was engaged by Jindal Stainless Limited (the ‘Company’) to conduct an independent assurance of the Company’s Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) (the ‘Report’) for the reporting period of April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. SGS India has conducted a Reasonable level of Assurance for the BRSR Report (BRSR core and non-Core indicators against all 9 principles), including essential and leadership indicators and all disclosures made thereunder. This assurance engagement was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements (ISAE) 3000 (Revised) and ISAE 3410. 

### **Reporting Framework** 

The Report has been prepared following 

1. Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 by listed entities. (Circular: HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD POD2/I/3762/2026; Last updated on Jan 30, 2026) 

2. GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard 

### **Intended Users of this Assurance Statement** 

This Assurance Statement is provided with the intention of informing all Company’s internal and external Stakeholders. 

### **Responsibilities** 

The information in the report and its presentation is the responsibility of the management of the Company. SGS India has not been involved in the preparation of any of the material included in the report. 

Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the text, data, and statements within the defined scope of assurance, aiming to inform the management of the Company, and in alignment with the agreed terms of reference. We do not accept or assume any responsibility beyond this specific scope. The Statement shall not be used for interpreting the overall performance of the Company, except for the aspects explicitly mentioned within the scope. 

### **Assurance Standard** 

SGS India has conducted a Reasonable level of Assurance for BRSR core parameters under 9 ESG Attributes and the remaining non-core parameters under 9 BRSR principles, including all essential and leadership indicators as specified under BRSR standards and amendments made as on date. This engagement was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagement (ISAE) 3000 (revised) and ISAE 3410 (Assurance Engagements other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information). 

Our evidence-gathering procedures were designed to obtain a ‘Reasonable’ level of assurance, which is a high level of assurance (BRSR Core) and “Reasonable” level of assurance which is high level of assurance (for BRSR Non-core) in accordance with ISAE

# **Statement of Independence and Competence** 

The SGS Group of companies is the world leader in inspection, testing, and assurance, operating in more than 140 countries and providing services including management systems and service certification; quality, environmental, social, and ethical auditing and training; and environmental, social, and sustainability report assurance. SGS India affirms our independence from Jindal Stainless Limited, being free from bias and conflicts of interest with the organization, its subsidiaries, and stakeholders. 

The assurance team was assembled based on their knowledge, experience, and qualifications for this assignment, and comprised auditors registered with ISO 26000, ISO 20121, ISO 50001, SA8000, RBA, QMS, EMS, SMS, GPMS, CFP, WFP, GHG Verification, and GHG Validation Lead Auditors, and experience on the SRA Assurance. 

# **Scope of Assurance** 

The assurance process involved assessing the quality, accuracy, and reliability of BRSR Indicators, including all KPI’s within the report for the period April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. The reporting scope and boundaries are on a standalone basis: 

On-site verification of data and internal controls at the following manufacturing locations: 

- JSL, Jajpur, Odisha (Manufacturing site) 

- JSL, Hisar, Haryana (Manufacturing site) 

Virtual verification through screen sharing tools at the following locations: 

- JSL, Jindal Centre, New Delhi (Corporate Office) 

- JSL Service Centers 

- JSL Stockyards 

# **Assurance Methodology** 

The assurance comprised a combination of desktop review, interaction with the key personnel engaged in the process of developing the report, on-site visits, and remote verification of data. Specifically, SGS India undertook the following activities: 

- Assessment of the suitability of the applicable criteria in terms of their comprehensiveness, reliability, and accuracy. 

- Interaction with key personnel responsible for collecting, consolidating, and calculating the BRSR core, and non-core indicators, and assessing the internal control mechanisms in place to ensure data quality. 

- Application of analytical procedures and verification of documents on a sample basis for the compilation and reporting of the KPIs. 

- Assessing the aggregation process of data at the Head Office level. 

- Critical review of the report regarding the plausibility and consistency of qualitative and quantitative information related to the KPIs. 

# **Limitations** 

SGS India did not come across any limitation to the agreed scope of the assurance engagement. SGS India verified data on a sample basis; the responsibility for the authenticity of the data entirely lies with the Company. The assurance scope excluded forward-looking statements, product- or service-related information, external information sources, and expert opinions. SGS India has not been involved in the evaluation or assessment of any financial data/performance of the company. Our opinion on financial indicators is based on the third-party financial reports audited by the Company. SGS India does not take any responsibility for the financial data reported in the audited financial reports of the Company.

# Management Discussion & Analysis 



# Global Economy 

The global economy remained broadly stable during CY25 despite facing multiple challenges, including geopolitical tensions, persistent inflationary pressures, uneven demand recovery, and evolving trade dynamics. Global GDP growth stood at 3.4% in CY25, supported by the resilience of emerging markets and a gradual improvement in economic activity across advanced economies. 

A key structural driver of global economic growth in CY25 was the sharp acceleration in AI-related investments, primarily led by the United States and select Asian economies. This momentum was enhanced by sustained technology investments, supported by rising hyperscaler capital expenditure, semiconductor capacity expansion, and the rapid development of data centres and cloud infrastructure. Against this backdrop, advanced economies recorded growth of 1.9% during the year, with the United States remaining a key contributor. The Euro Area also experienced a gradual recovery, supported by moderating inflation, stabilising energy markets, and improving consumer confidence. 

The United States economy remained resilient despite high interest rates and tighter financial conditions, supported by continued infrastructure spending, manufacturing activity, 

and private investment. Meanwhile, Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDEs) grew by 4.4%, outperforming advanced economies. Asia remained the primary growth engine; China recorded 5.0% growth, supported by strong exports and manufacturing activity. However, weak domestic demand and continued challenges in the property sector moderated its overall growth. Meanwhile, India remained the fastest-growing major economy in 2025 with 7.1% growth, supported by strong domestic consumption, sustained public infrastructure spending, expanding manufacturing activity, and a resilient services sector. Government initiatives focused on infrastructure development, industrial growth, and ease of doing business continued to strengthen economic momentum, reinforcing India’s position as a key driver of global growth. 

Despite the improvement in global economic conditions, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the broader West Asia region continued to create uncertainty during CY25 and early CY26. Concerns over possible disruptions to key trade routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, led to fluctuations in crude oil prices and shipping costs. In addition, higher tariffs, supply chain disruptions, and tighter financial conditions continued to affect global trade and business confidence.

## Outlook 

Central banks across major economies maintained a cautious and increasingly divergent monetary policy stance. In the United States, the Federal Reserve is poised to gradually reduce interest rates, with the federal funds rate projected to decline to around 3.1% by CY27 from 3.50%–3.75% in mid CY26. In Europe, the ECB kept its benchmark policy rate at 2.15%, alongside a 2% deposit rate and a 2.40% marginal lending rate. In Japan, interest rates are projected to rise gradually toward 1.5% as the country continues to normalise monetary policy. Central banks across emerging economies complemented interest rate actions with targeted foreign exchange and liquidity measures to contain currency volatility and preserve financial system stability. At the same time, structural growth drivers remained intact, with AI-driven capital expenditure expected to support productivity gains and sustained investment in compute-intensive infrastructure. This is also likely to increase electricity demand, reinforcing the energy intensity of digital economies and creating new investment opportunities despite a challenging macroeconomic environment. 

Looking ahead, global economic conditions are projected to remain unsettled, shaped by ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, policy caution, and uneven growth across major economies. Crude oil prices are likely to remain volatile but broadly range-bound, with episodic spikes driven by geopolitical shocks, while underlying demand 

from EMDEs provides a structural floor. In parallel, energy markets are likely to remain sensitive to supply-side disruptions, with implications for inflation dynamics, trade balances, and the fiscal positions of oil-importing economies, particularly in Asia. 

Global growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in CY26, reflecting prolonged geopolitical risks, trade disruptions, and subdued momentum in key economies. Advanced economies are expected to grow by 1.8% in CY26 and by 1.7% in CY27. Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDEs) are projected to grow by 3.9% in CY26 and 4.1% in CY27, continuing to serve as key drivers of global economic activity. Among major economies, India is expected to maintain its position as the fastest-growing large economy, with GDP growth projected at around 6.5% in both CY26 and CY27, supported by strong domestic consumption, sustained infrastructure investments, manufacturing expansion, and ongoing policy reforms. The pace of global growth will largely depend on monetary policy developments, geopolitical conditions, and the resilience of consumer spending, and business investment across major economies.

# Indian Economy 

India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies in FY26, supported by strong domestic demand, a young workforce, and ongoing structural reforms. As per the Provisional Estimates released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), under the revised FY23 base-year series, India’s GDP is estimated to have grown by 7.7% in FY26, compared with 7.1% in FY25. The growth reflects the resilience of the Indian economy, aided by robust domestic demand, investment activity, and a strong services sector despite a challenging global environment. This growth was largely driven by steady consumption trends, persistent government-led infrastructure investment, and improving industrial activity across key sectors.

# Outlook 

Despite external challenges such as elevated commodity prices, periodic supply disruptions, variable monsoon conditions, and uneven global demand, India’s economic outlook remains firmly supported by strong domestic demand, sustained investment activity, resilient services exports, and proactive policy measures that continue to strengthen overall economic stability. Inflation is expected to edge up to 5.1% in FY27 from 3.4% in FY26, primarily driven by higher prices of commercial LPG, base metals, plastics, and rubber, indicating broader pass-through of input costs alongside steady demand conditions. 

The FY27 Union Budget supports India’s long-term manufacturing ambitions through focused measures across strategic sectors such as advanced manufacturing, capital goods, semiconductors, chemicals, electronics, and industrial infrastructure. Alongside initiatives such as the National Manufacturing Mission, industrial corridors, PM GatiShakti, logistics reforms, and PLI schemes, these measures are expected to strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities, enhance supply-chain resilience, and catalyse private sector investment. This momentum is further aided by rapid digital adoption, particularly through platforms like UPI, which continue to improve transaction efficiency, formalisation, and financial inclusion. Moreover, sustained demand for India’s technology and business services in global markets is projected to accelerate services exports, strengthening the country’s external account and overall economic momentum.

# Industry Overview 

## Global Stainless Steel Industry 

The stainless steel industry remains a key contributor to global industrial and infrastructure development, supported by rising demand for durable, corrosion-resistant, and sustainable materials. Between 1980 and 2023, global stainless steel consumption grew at a 5.10% CAGR by volume, making it the fastest-growing major metal over the past four decades. This growth, well above the average of 2.36% for major metals, has been driven by increasing use across construction, transportation, manufacturing, and consumer applications.

India is expected to remain the fastest-growing major stainless steel market, driven by investments in infrastructure, construction, transportation, manufacturing, and capital goods. Among developed markets, the United States is likely to benefit from infrastructure spending and supportive industrial policies, while Europe’s recovery will depend on energy costs, regulatory developments, and the pace of industrial activity. The growing emphasis on higher recycled content and lower-emission production is also expected to strengthen its role in supporting the transition to a circular and lowcarbon economy. 

At the same time, the global trade environment is becoming increasingly policy-driven. Countries are adopting measures such as higher tariffs, import quotas, safeguard duties, and carbon-related trade regulations to protect domestic industries and strengthen supply chain resilience. In Europe, trade continues to be influenced by EU’s safeguard quota mechanism, which restricts imports beyond country-specific tariff-rate quotas. While the implementation of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is reshaping stainless steel trade by introducing carbon-linked costs on imports, encouraging lower-emission production and influencing global sourcing decisions. In the United States, the increase in steel import tariffs under Section 232 from 25% to 50% on June 4, 2025, is expected to continue to support domestic producers while redirecting global trade flows, encouraging exporters to diversify into alternative markets and increasing competitive intensity across international markets. Despite these evolving trade dynamics, the industry’s strong demand fundamentals and expanding application base are expected to support sustainable long-term growth.

# Indian Stainless Steel Industry 

India continues to strengthen its position as one of the world’s fastest-growing stainless steel markets and is expected to remain the second-largest globally over the next several years, supported by evolving demand segments and policy enablers. 

The industry will also benefit from policy support, including the latest phase of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme 1.2 for specialty steel, which aims to promote domestic manufacturing of higher-value steel products, reduce import dependence, and encourage technology upgrades. For the stainless steel sector, the scheme is expected to support capacity expansion, product diversification, and the development of value-added grades, thereby improving India’s competitiveness in global markets. 

Stainless steel is widely used for its strength, durability, and corrosion resistance. It can also withstand heat and requires low maintenance over its lifetime. These qualities make it an important material for transportation networks, industrial facilities, commercial buildings, process industries, and consumer applications. 

India continued to witness steady growth in stainless steel consumption during FY26, supported by infrastructure development, industrial expansion, urbanisation, and increasing adoption across diverse applications. According to the Indian Stainless Steel Development Association (ISSDA), domestic stainless steel consumption increased to 5.16 MT in FY26 from 4.8 MT in FY25, compared with 3.50 MT in FY20, highlighting the industry’s consistent growth over the years.

As the world’s second-largest consumer of stainless steel, India continues to see rising demand across infrastructure, transportation, construction, and manufacturing, while new applications in green hydrogen, food processing, pharmaceuticals and other emerging industries are creating additional growth opportunities. At present, India’s per capita stainless steel consumption remains at approximately 3.6 kg, significantly below the global average of about 7 kg, indicating substantial headroom for future growth. With increasing collaboration between industry and policymakers to strengthen innovation, policy support, and market development, the Indian stainless steel industry remains wellpositioned to enhance its global competitiveness and sustain long-term growth. 

Growth is attributed to rising demand from a wide range of industrial applications, including transportation, engineering, food processing, water infrastructure, renewable energy, and process industries. Additionally, the increasing focus on sustainability, resource efficiency, and durable materials is expected to support stainless steel consumption. Among product categories, the 300-series grades are likely to continue accounting for the largest share of demand, owing to their versatility, superior corrosion resistance, recyclability, and extensive use across industrial, infrastructure, and consumer applications.

During the latter part of FY26, however, domestic production was affected by the limited availability of industrial gases such as LPG, propane and natural gas, leading to rationalised plant utilisation. The impact was more pronounced for scrapbased producers that are more dependent on externally sourced fuels than integrated production facilities. 

Industry stakeholders continue to focus on strengthening India’s stainless steel ecosystem through policy support, innovation, technology adoption, and enhanced market opportunities. With favourable demand fundamentals, expanding end-use applications, and significant headroom for higher consumption, India’s stainless steel industry remains well-positioned for long-term sustainable growth. 

The Quality Control Order (QCO) framework has been introduced to strengthen quality standards and curb the import of inferior and substandard stainless steel products into India. The Government provided a temporary exemption from QCO compliance requirements for finished stainless flat steel products effective from April 2026 until September 2026. Subsequently, in June 2026, the exemption period was further extended through March 31, 2027. Further, the implementation of QCO norms for input materials used in manufacturing these Stainless steel products deferred until September 30, 2026. 

Global overcapacity and diversion of trade flows to India arising from global protectionism have intensified competitive pressures on domestic manufacturers. Continued monitoring of imports and policy measures aimed at promoting fair trade are further to support a more balanced and sustainable market environment. 

Geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East, had added uncertainty to global energy markets and industrial operations. These disruptions affected the supply and pricing of key industrial gases such as LPG, propane, and natural gas, which are essential inputs for stainless steel production, especially for scrap-based units. In late FY26, limited availability of these fuels led to reduced plant utilisation.

# Sector-Specific Demand 

The Indian stainless steel industry continues to witness steady demand across infrastructure, construction, transportation, industrial processing, and consumer-oriented sectors. Large-scale investments in railways, metro systems, airports, water infrastructure, and urban development projects, along with growing adoption across automotive, EV, pipes and tubes, process industries and power generation, are supporting stainless steel consumption. 

In the consumer segment, rising urbanisation and improving living standards are driving demand for applications such as kitchenware, home appliances, elevators, and architectural fittings. At the same time, emerging sectors such as renewable energy, green hydrogen, defence, aerospace, and advanced engineering are creating new avenues for growth, further strengthening stainless steel’s position as a preferred material across India’s growth sectors. 

Amid this shift towards higher-value applications, JSL’s focus on value-added products and specialty grades remains a key differentiator. A greater share of such products in the sales mix enhances product positioning, improves pricing resilience, and supports a more stable earnings profile by reducing exposure to commodity steel price cycles. 

## Automotive, Railways and Transportation (ART) 

The ART sector remained a key driver of demand for the Indian stainless steel industry. Growing investments in railway modernisation, metro rail networks, freight wagons, urban mobility infrastructure, and automotive manufacturing are aiding demand for stainless steel products. Its superior corrosion resistance, durability, strength, low maintenance requirements, and recyclability make stainless steel an ideal material. As India accelerates investments in mobility and logistics infrastructure, the ART segment is expected to remain an important source of demand for higher-value stainless steel grades, supporting long-term industry growth and increased value addition. 

Government initiatives such as PM Gati Shakti, the National Logistics Policy, Bharatmala, Sagarmala, and railway modernisation programmes are expected to drive significant investments in transportation and logistics infrastructure. Supported by expanding rail, metro, freight, and commercial vehicle networks, stainless steel adoption is increasing owing to its superior strength, durability, and lifecycle benefits. These developments are expected to sustain demand for value-added stainless steel products across the automobile, railway, and transportation sectors. 

Indian Railways is also advancing clean rail transportation through hydrogen-powered train. The pilot project combines hydrogen fuel cell-based propulsion with dedicated hydrogen storage, refuelling and operational infrastructure,

demonstrating the feasibility of a train that generates electricity onboard using hydrogen. Additionally, the growing focus on sustainable mobility and EVs is likely to further strengthen demand, supporting the industry’s long-term growth prospects. 

## Automotive 

The Indian automotive industry maintained strong growth momentum during FY26, creating a favourable demand environment for stainless steel across automotive and mobility applications. Total vehicle production reached approximately 34.7 million units, supported by robust domestic demand across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, two-wheelers, and three-wheelers. The industry also recorded its highest-ever sales of 46.43 lakh units, representing a 7.9% Y-O-Y increase. Growth was underpinned by strong consumer demand, supportive policy measures, improving economic activity, rising infrastructure spending, increased logistics activity, and ongoing fleet modernisation. 

The automotive sector remained a significant driver of stainless steel demand, with two-wheelers and passenger vehicles accounting for nearly 85-90% of industry consumption within the segment. Increasing emphasis on vehicle safety, stringent emission norms, durability, corrosion resistance, and lightweighting is expected to further enhance stainless steel intensity per vehicle, supporting demand for high-performance grades used in chassis systems, structural components, and emission-control applications. 

India’s accelerating transition towards electric mobility presents an additional avenue for stainless steel demand growth. EV adoption continued to gather pace during FY26, with passenger EV registrations increasing by over 80% compared to the previous year. As automakers focus on sustainable manufacturing and advanced vehicle technologies, stainless steel is expected to play an increasingly important role in the next phase of the automotive industry’s growth. 

Looking ahead, the Indian automotive industry is expected to maintain steady growth in FY27, Continued premiumisation, increasing EV penetration, and sustained replacement demand are likely to support stainless steel consumption across a wide range of automotive applications. 

During FY26, Jindal Stainless (JSL) further strengthened its presence in the transportation segment through the launch of its Stainless Steel Salt Tipper Trailer in Gujarat. Developed using advanced 304 and JT (N7) grades, the solution is specifically designed for salt transportation and offers nearly 25% lower weight along with a significantly longer service life compared to conventional alternatives. This initiative underscores the Company’s focus on

# Railways 

Indian Railways remains one of the largest and most important demand drivers for the stainless steel industry. As the railway network expands and modernises, stainless steel is finding wider use across passenger coaches, metro trains, high-speed rail systems, wagons, station infrastructure, and freight facilities. 

The rising adoption of modern rolling stock, such as LHB coaches, Vande Bharat, and Amrit Bharat trains, is significantly increasing stainless steel consumption across the railway sector. Stainless steel is widely used in coach structures, interiors, sanitary systems, and safety components. It is also expanding into freight wagons, cargo infrastructure, metro projects, and station redevelopment due to its durability and ability to perform under heavy-duty operating conditions. 

As of March 2026, the network has achieved over 99% electrification, freight loading of around 1,650 MT, and nearly 2,800 km of Dedicated Freight Corridors are operational. With around 48,000 Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches, over 160 Vande Bharat trains and about 60 Amrit Bharat trains, along with a rapidly expanding metro network, the sector remains a key long-term driver of stainless steel demand.

# Transport 

The Indian road transport and highway sector is witnessing sustained capacity expansion, creating strong long-term demand for stainless steel across transport infrastructure and logistics ecosystems. India’s highway sector has expanded significantly, with the length of National Highways increasing from 91,287 km in FY14 to 1,46,572 km in FY26. 

As infrastructure quality improves, the use of stainless steel is steadily increasing in bridges, highways, crash barriers, flyovers, toll plazas, drainage systems, signage and urban mobility assets, driven by its corrosion resistance, durability, and low maintenance requirements. It is also gaining importance in logistics parks, multimodal hubs, and wayside amenities, where long service life, safety, and hygiene are critical. 

This shift is further supported by the development of accesscontrolled expressways and high-speed corridors. During this transition, four-lane-and-above highways have expanded from 18,371 km to 48,568 km, while access-controlled corridors have increased from 93 km to about 3,052 km. 

cargo-handling structures, fuel stations, and allied support infrastructure. The recyclability and sustainability credentials of the material also align well with modern infrastructure development priorities, particularly in projects focused on efficiency, lower lifecycle costs, and improved environmental performance. 

Sustained government policy support, strong domestic demand, and projected infrastructure investments are expected to support stainless steel consumption across construction, transportation, and energy applications.

# Nuclear Power Plants 

Stainless steel is one of the most essential materials in nuclear power generation, as its unique properties enable safe, reliable, and long-term plant operation. Nuclear reactors rely extensively on stainless steel in supercritical boilers, reactor vessels, high-pressure piping and cooling equipment, storage tanks, chimneys, and structural components. 

It is widely used in the construction of reactor pressure vessels, which must withstand extreme pressure, temperature, and radiation over long operational lifetimes. Stainless steel also plays a critical role in spent fuel storage casks, ensuring secure containment and effective radiation shielding for safe long-term storage. In advanced nuclear applications such as fusion reactors, it is used in magnetic coils and structural components, providing essential thermal stability and mechanical strength. 

Looking ahead, India has set an ambitious target of 100 GW of nuclear capacity by 2047 under the Nuclear Energy Mission, with an INR 20,000 crore investment under the FY26 Union Budget, including the development of Small Modular Reactors (at least five by 2033), advanced reactor designs, and high-temperature gas-cooled reactors. As India advances its plans to significantly expand nuclear power generation capacity in the coming years, demand for stainless steel is projected to grow, led by its extensive use in critical nuclear infrastructure and equipment.

# Fertiliser and Paper Industries 

The fertiliser and paper industries are key end-use sectors for stainless steel, given their reliance on process equipment operating under corrosive, high-temperature, and highpressure conditions. 

In the fertiliser sector, stainless steel is widely used in ammonia, urea, nitric acid, and phosphoric acid plants, finding applications in reactors, synthesis towers, condensers, scrubbers, stripping towers, pipelines, storage tanks, heat exchangers, and valves. Different grades, including specialised urea-grade, duplex, and high-alloy stainless steels, are used in critical process equipment to improve plant reliability, operational efficiency, and equipment life. 

Similarly, the paper industry remains a significant consumer of stainless steel across pulp and paper manufacturing processes. Stainless steel is extensively used in digesters, evaporators, pulp-processing equipment, storage tanks, pumps, valves, screens, conveyor systems, rollers, and drying cylinders. Modern paper mills are increasingly adopting stainless steel in critical equipment as they invest in technology upgrades, capacity expansion, and more efficient production systems. 

Looking ahead, both industries are anticipated to remain important drivers of stainless steel demand in India. Continued investments in fertiliser production capacity, agricultural infrastructure, paper manufacturing facilities, and packaging applications are expected to support longterm growth.

# Outlook 

The Indian stainless steel industry is poised for strong long-term growth, supported by the country’s economic expansion, rapid urbanisation, increasing infrastructure development, and continued growth in manufacturing. As India progresses towards its vision of becoming a developed economy by 2047, demand for stainless steel is poised to increase across a wide range of sectors, including construction, transportation, energy, engineering, consumer goods, and process industries. 

Government initiatives such as PM GatiShakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme are driving large-scale investments in railways, roads, metros, airports, water infrastructure, logistics, and industrial manufacturing. These investments are creating significant opportunities for stainless steel due to its corrosion resistance, durability, strength, and sustainability. Continued government capital expenditure across these sectors is anticipated to support steady growth in stainless steel consumption over the coming years.

At the same time, new-age sectors such as renewable energy, green hydrogen, electric mobility, aerospace, defence, and advanced manufacturing are creating opportunities for specialised, value-added stainless steel products. The National Green Hydrogen Mission, with an outlay of around INR 20,000 crore, aims to establish India as a global hub for the production, use, and export of green hydrogen and its derivatives. Demand is also rising from industries such as food processing, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, chemicals, and consumer appliances, resulting in a more diversified and resilient demand base. 

According to industry estimates, India’s stainless steel consumption is likely to grow at around 7–8% annually over the medium term, outpacing global growth rates. Domestic consumption is projected to increase to 12.5–12.7 MT by FY40 and further to 19–20 MT by FY47, driven by rising infrastructure investments, manufacturing activities, and higher per capita usage. 

Looking ahead, the industry’s outlook remains positive, aided by stable demand, ongoing infrastructure development, and an increasing focus on sustainable growth. As a fully recyclable material that plays a critical role in modern infrastructure, manufacturing, and clean energy applications, stainless steel is poised to remain an important contributor to India’s next phase of economic and industrial development.

# Green and Sustainable Wonder Metal 

Stainless steel has long been valued as the ‘wonder metal’ for its infinite recyclability, durability, and corrosion resistance. Jindal Stainless is sharpening that inherent sustainability edge into a dedicated product offering, in line with India’s evolving green steel policy landscape. Anchored in the country’s Net Zero-by-2070 commitment, this regulatory push will give JSL a clear domestic mandate, alongside global customer expectations, to build verifiable, low-carbon product lines ahead of the curve. 

In response, JSL is developing a sustainable stainlesssteel product line, built around selected 300-series grades manufactured with a minimum certified recycled content of 90%. Produced through the Company’s  electric-arcfurnace-based route, this line will deliver 60-70% lower carbon emissions compared to the conventional production pathway, along with lower lifecycle energy consumption, a reduced water footprint, and a smaller ecological footprint. This will also give the customers a quantifiable lever to 

reduce their Scope 3 value-chain emissions and meet their sustainability targets. 

Beyond the product itself, the Company is building the ecosystem around it and supporting customers in navigating green procurement frameworks, reinforced by third-party certification of recycled content, and going forward, product carbon footprint (PCF) verification. This next phase reflects JSL’s broader ambition—a 50% reduction in carbon emission intensity before FY35 and net zero by 2050—and reinforces its commitment to staying ahead of evolving global greensteel definitions. As more customers adopt science-based decarbonisation targets, JSL is positioned to become their preferred low-carbon stainless steel partner.

# Policy & Regulatory Developments 

## 1.  Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme 1.2 for Specialty Steel 

The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme is strengthening India’s specialty steel ecosystem through investments of around INR 23,022 crore, supporting domestic production, capacity expansion, and import substitution. The latest phase, PLI 1.2, is projected to add about 8.29 MT of capacity through investments of INR 11,887 crore. For the stainless steel industry, this is expected to support the development of advanced and value-added grades. It will also strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities. In addition, it is likely to increase opportunities across sectors such as infrastructure, mobility, engineering, and clean energy. As part of this initiative, Jindal Stainless has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) under the PLI 1.2 scheme to expand its specialty steel capabilities. 

## 2. Coastal Infrastructure 

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has mandated the use of high-tensile stainless steel in bridges and infrastructure in coastal and marineexposed areas, expanding coverage beyond the earlier 15-km coastal zone to wider saltwater-affected regions. Although initial costs may rise by 10–15%, stainless steel significantly extends the structure’s life up to 75 years and reduces maintenance costs by nearly 50%. The move supports the government’s focus on evaluating infrastructure projects based on lifecycle costs rather than initial capital expenditure alone. This is particularly relevant for India’s 11,098.81 km coastline and major projects such as the Mumbai Coastal Road, Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, Vizhinjam Deep-Sea Port, Vadhavan Port, and the Sagarmala Programme, further driving strong demand for durable materials. 

## 3. Infrastructure Push 

The FY27 Union Budget has increased infrastructure capex by 9% to INR 12.2 lakh crore, supporting strong demand for steel and stainless steel across railways, metros, airports, highways, and urban transport systems. This sustained spending, along with duty rationalisation on key raw materials such as ferrous scrap, has improved availability and strengthened cost competitiveness for the stainless steel industry. Overall, various government programmes continue to indirectly 

support demand for stainless steel through large-scale infrastructure development. 

## 4. Quality-Led Industry Growth 

The Government of India (GoI) has established a policy framework comprising Quality Control Orders (QCOs), and the Steel Import Monitoring System (SIMS) to ensure quality standards, promote domestic manufacturing, and reduce import dependence. QCOs aim to ensure the use of quality-compliant stainless steel in India across all applications while encouraging domestic manufacturers to enhance their capacities, quality and curb the import of inferior and substandard stainless steel products into India. The government provided a temporary exemption from QCO compliance requirements for finished stainless flat steel products effective from April 2026 until September 2026. Subsequently, in June 2026, the exemption period was further extended through March 31, 2027. Further, the implementation of QCO norms for input materials used in manufacturing these stainless steel products deferred until September 30, 2026. This development may lead to an increase in inflows of lower-priced sub-standard imports, potentially affecting domestic capacity utilisation and long-term industry growth. 

## 5. National Stainless Steel Policy 

Given the distinct characteristics and strategic importance of the stainless steel sector, the industry has advocated a dedicated National Stainless Steel Policy. Such a policy would provide a long-term roadmap for capacity creation, raw material security, and consumption growth, while reducing import dependence and enhancing the global competitiveness of domestic producers. It would also support a more resilient and self-reliant stainless steel value chain, aligned with India’s manufacturing ambitions.

# Threats 

3. Sub-standard Imports and QCO Relaxation: The temporary relaxation of Quality Control Order (QCO) requirements has increased the risk of sub-standard stainless steel products entering the domestic market. The influx of non-compliant imports can adversely impact domestic capacity utilisation, discourage investments in quality enhancement and technological advancement, and compromise consumer interests by increasing the availability of inferior products. 

The stainless steel industry faces several external and structural threats that continue to affect its cost structure, competitiveness, and capacity utilisation. 

1. Raw Material Dependence and Price Volatility: The stainless steel industry remains heavily dependent on imported raw materials such as nickel, stainless steel scrap, ferroalloys, chromium, and molybdenum. Prices of these key inputs are inherently volatile due to geopolitical developments, mining regulations, currency fluctuations, and supply-demand imbalances. Additionally, dependence on imports exposes the industry to global supply disruptions, logistics constraints, and foreign exchange risks, which can impact production planning, cost stability, and profitability. 

   4. Inequitable Trade Access, including the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and US Tariffs: Evolving global trade regulations, tariffs, free trade agreements, and tariff-rate quotas continue to create an uncertain operating environment. Recent tariff and quota measures in key export markets, including the United States and the European Union, have led to a realignment of trade flows. These measures have diverted exports from the US and EU toward, relatively unprotected and fast-growing markets such as India. At the same time, geopolitical tensions continue to disrupt supply routes and affect pricing stability. 

2. Import Competition and Global Overcapacity: Global stainless steel markets continue to face structural overcapacity, particularly in China and ASEAN, resulting in persistent pricing pressure and intensified competition. Low-cost imports, including Chinese-origin material routed through ASEAN countries under Free Trade Agreement (FTA) channels, have increased their presence in the Indian market, impacting domestic capacity utilisation and pricing. The challenge is further compounded by dumping practices, subsidies, and lower compliance costs in certain regions, affecting the competitiveness of domestic manufacturers.

# Company Overview 

## About Jindal Stainless Limited 



Jindal Stainless Ltd. (hereafter referred to as ‘JSL’ or ‘the Company’), established in 1970, is India’s leading stainless steel manufacturer with a strong presence across domestic and international markets. The Company also ranks among the top three stainless steel producers globally. The Company has built its reputation through continuous innovation, ethical business practices, strong customer relationships, and the dedication of its employees. 

JSL operates 16 stainless steel manufacturing and processing facilities across India, Spain, and Indonesia as of March 2026, and has established a global footprint in 12 countries. JSL has also strengthened its domestic reach through a network of 10 sales offices and six service centres across India. The Company has key manufacturing facilities in India at Jajpur, Hisar, and through its Subsidiary, Chromeni Steels at Mundra . Internationally, it operates a Steel Melt Shop (SMS) and an NPI facility in Indonesia. These plants together support large-scale production, improve efficiency, and strengthen its global supply chain. 

JSL strengthened its brand presence in FY26 through a nationwide multimedia campaign aimed at deepening consumer connect and expanding engagement across younger and mass-market audiences, enhancing overall brand visibility and recall. 

JSL remains focused on sustainable manufacturing, with electric arc furnaces (EAFs) and scrap-based production forming the core of its operations. Scrap accounted for nearly 70% of the total input, reducing emissions and promoting recyclability in FY26. The Company has also committed to reducing its carbon emissions intensity by 50% by FY35 and aims to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. 

JSL maintains a strong focus on safety, quality, and efficient operations as it continues to advance its manufacturing base. The Company operates through a fully integrated business model that supports efficient operations and cost competitiveness. JSL continues to invest in growth and innovation to strengthen its market position, create long-term value, and build brand equity as stainless steel adoption expands across a growing range of applications in India. 

In addition, the Company aims to achieve sales volumes of 3.5 MTPA by FY29, up from 2.57 MTPA in FY26, which is expected to drive strong double-digit compounded growth over the next few years. 

### Product Portfolio 

JSL is India’s largest stainless steel producer and one of the leading manufacturers globally, offering a comprehensive range of products for diverse industrial and end-use applications. The Company’s product basket includes stainless steel slabs, blooms, coils, plates, sheets, precision strips, wire rods, rebars, blade steel, and coin blanks, manufactured across the 200, 300, and 400 series and duplex grades. With a portfolio comprising more than 120 grades, the Company serves a broad spectrum of sectors, including infrastructure, railways, automotive, process industries, architecture, renewable energy, consumer durables, and engineering applications. JSL achieved its 4.2 MT per annum (MTPA) capacity target ahead of schedule in FY26 with the commissioning of a 1.2 MTPA facility in Indonesia. 

The Company is supported by healthy demand from the automotive, pipes and tubes, metro projects, lifts and elevators, and white goods sectors. Growth was further driven by the increasing adoption of stainless steel across infrastructure, electric vehicles, real estate, defence, aerospace, ethanol production, trailers, and container applications. Despite challenges arising from low-cost imports, trade-circumvention practices, and global trade uncertainties, JSL enhanced its competitive position by focusing on specialised, value-added offerings. 

JSL’s integrated manufacturing operations, extensive processing capabilities, and efficient supply chain network enable the delivery of high-quality, cost-effective, and sustainable stainless steel solutions. Its broad application across transportation, infrastructure, industrial equipment, consumer goods, defence and advanced engineering sectors, combined with its expanding global presence, positions the Company to capitalise on emerging growth opportunities in India and overseas markets.

# Key Business Initiatives 

## Expansion of Slag Processing Capacity at Jajpur 

JSL is doubling its slag processing capacity at its Jajpur facility through a new wet milling plant in partnership with Harsco Environmental, aimed at strengthening circular production and recovering metals from industrial waste. The project, involving an investment of USD 150 million under a 15-year agreement, will also enhance resource efficiency and support long-term sustainability goals. 

## Commissioning of Indonesia Melt Shop 

In March 2026, JSL commissioned its 1.2 MTPA stainless steel melt shop in Indonesia through its joint venture operations, ahead of schedule, marking a significant milestone in its capacity expansion strategy. With this commissioning, the Company’s total stainless steel melting capacity has increased to 4.2 MTPA, including 3 MTPA in India. The output material from the Indonesia melt shop will be further processed in India through Hot Rolling Annealing and Pickling (HRAP) facility and Cold Rolling Annealing and Pickling (CRAP) facility to manufacture finished stainless steel products. This integrated expansion strengthens JSL’s global supply chain, enhances operational flexibility and supports its long-term growth strategy. 

## Scaling Renewable Energy for Sustainable Manufacturing 

JSL, in partnership with AB Energia Solutions Pvt. Ltd., commissioned Odisha’s largest captive industrial solar power plant at its Jajpur facility, with a total capacity of over 30 Megawatt-peak (MWp). The project comprises a 7.324 MWp floating solar installation and a 23.02 MWp rooftop solar system, enabling annual generation of approximately 44.3 Million Units (MU) of green energy annually. This initiative significantly reduces dependence on grid electricity, and is likely to cut CO2 emissions by around 32,208 metric tonnes annually. 

The project marks a key milestone in the Company’s Net Zero 2050 journey and accelerates its commitment to large-scale renewable energy adoption and sustainable manufacturing. Jindal Stainless has partnered with Oyster Renewable Energy to develop a 315.6 MW solar-wind hybrid renewable energy project in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, at an investment of of INR 132 crore by the Company. The project, once fully operational, is expected to enable Jindal Stainless to abate around 6.5 lakh metric tonnes of carbon emissions per year, while reinforcing the growing importance of hybrid renewable solutions in delivering reliable clean power to energyintensive industries.

## Raw Material related Initiatives 

- Scrap-led sourcing: JSL has increased its focus on scrap-based inputs, with around 70–72% of raw materials sourced from scrap. This reduces dependence on mined resources and helps lower exposure to volatile nickel and ore prices. JSL is increasing the use of recycled and domestic scrap, including auto scrap tie-ups, thereby supporting cost efficiency and improving sustainability. 

- Domestic and Near-Shore Sourcing: The Company is sourcing more materials from domestic and nearby suppliers to reduce logistics costs, avoid import delays, and improve supply reliability. 

- Diversification of Suppliers: JSL is working with a broader base of suppliers rather than relying on a few large ones. This helps reduce procurement risk and improves flexibility in buying raw materials. 

- Centralised Procurement: JSL manages its procurement through a central system, which helps optimise costs by enabling better supplier evaluation, bulk buying, and structured cost monitoring. 

- Mining-led Raw Material Security: The Company is strengthening long-term raw material security through strategic backward integration initiatives, including chrome ore linkage with Odisha Mining Corporation (OMC) and the development of captive mining assets at Sukinda, enhancing supply reliability and reducing dependence on external sources. 

- Nickel Supply Diversification (NPI – Indonesia): JSL’s 49% stake in an Indonesia-based NPI joint venture strengthens backward integration by securing a reliable source of nickel, enhancing supply stability, and reinforcing long-term raw material security 

- Capacity Expansion & Manufacturing Diversification (SMS – Indonesia): JSL’s 49% stake in an Indonesiabased stainless steel melt shop (SMS) strengthens its global manufacturing footprint, increasing melting capacity by over 40% to 4.2 MTPA. The facility diversifies production through the NPI route and enhances supply security for downstream operations.

JSL’s Stainless Academy is an education and skilling platform aimed at strengthening India’s stainless steel ecosystem. The Academy promotes awareness of stainless steel and builds industry-relevant capabilities among fabricators, students, technical professionals, manufacturers, and other ecosystem partners. It also works towards developing standardised training frameworks and academic curricula for the stainless steel industry.

# Risk and Mitigation Strategies 

Key Risks 

Raw Material Price Risk 

## Particulars 

Dependence on nickel, ferrochrome, and scrap prices exposes the Company to global commodity price volatility and supply fluctuations, which can impact raw material costs and margins. 

## Mitigation Strategy 

JSL mitigates nickel supply risks through diversified domestic and international sourcing, supported by long-term supplier partnerships and strategic tie-ups, including a joint venture to ensure secure availability of nickel pig iron. For ferrochrome, the Company follows a diversified sourcing approach, procuring raw materials through a mix of scrap, captive mines and supplies from Odisha Mining Corporation (OMC). Scrap is primarily sourced through domestic suppliers who procure material on behalf of JSL, while strategic supplier relationships help ensure consistent availability of key inputs. 

Import Risk 

Low-cost imports, especially from China and FTA-linked markets, create pricing pressure and affect domestic competitiveness. 

The Company focuses on developing new grades, expanding applications, and strengthening domestic demand. It also supports regulatory measures such as Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) standards and Quality Control Orders (QCOs) to ensure quality compliance and fair competition, while reducing import dependence through portfolio diversification. 

Supply Chain Risk 

Geopolitical tensions, natural disasters, and global disruptions may impact logistics and raw material availability. 

JSL maintains a diversified supplier base, increases domestic and regional sourcing, and follows a flexible procurement strategy to ensure supply continuity and operational resilience. 

Regulatory Risk 

Changes in environmental, product quality, and industry regulations may impact compliance requirements and operating costs. 

The Company proactively monitors regulatory changes, ensures early compliance readiness, and aligns with evolving standards. It also tracks and participates in discussions on emerging policy frameworks, including the proposed National Stainless Steel Policy.

# Mitigation Strategy 

JSL maintains disciplined leverage, optimises debt through refinancing and maturity management, and uses hedging strategies to manage currency risk while improving capital efficiency. 

The Company has implemented robust cybersecurity systems, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, regular security audits, employee training programmes, and structured incident response mechanisms to ensure data and operational security. 

Environmental & Climate Risk 

Regulatory shifts such as CBAM and dependence on imported critical inputs like nickel increase climate-related risks. 

JSL is investing in renewable energy, lowemission technologies, higher scrap usage, circular economy practices, and backward integration initiatives. It is also strengthening carbon accounting, emissions transparency, and evaluating future technologies such as green hydrogen and electrification to improve longterm sustainability and compliance readiness.

JSL believes that its people are at the heart of its long-term success and remains committed to creating a workplace that encourages growth, inclusivity and high performance. As of FY26, the Company employed more than 29,000 people and stayed focused on attracting, developing and retaining talent through structured hiring practices, leadership development programmes and continuous learning initiatives. Alongside this, JSL maintained a strong emphasis on employee engagement, workplace well-being and the development of a performance-driven culture.

The Company extended the programme beyond rewards by offering accidental life insurance coverage and access to fabrication training programmes. JSL aims to support skill development and encourage the adoption of genuine stainless steel products across the value chain through this initiative. 

JSL also enhanced workforce experience through technology-led HR transformation and greater use of digital platforms and AI-driven tools. The Company integrated AI across several HR functions, including talent acquisition, candidate screening, job description creation, employee engagement survey analysis and action plan recommendations. In addition, JSL developed an AI-enabled HR ecosystem that supports self-service capabilities, improves data-driven decision-making and strengthens inclusive employee engagement across multiple digital platforms, helping to promote a more collaborative and future-ready workplace. 

During the year, the Company continued to strengthen its Employee Value Proposition (EVP) by deepening investments in employee learning, growth, and career development. As part of this effort, JSL launched ASTRA, its Technical Academy, to build future-ready technical capabilities across the organisation. The Company also partnered with prestigious academic and industry institutions to strengthen Leadership Development and Functional Academies, providing structured development pathways for leadership and critical functional talent pools. In addition, JSL commenced its mentoring journey through ‘Prerna’, a structured mentoring programme aimed at fostering knowledge sharing, leadership development and career progression through meaningful mentor-mentee relationships. These initiatives further reinforced the Company’s EVP, which is anchored on five key pillars—learning opportunities, nurturing leaders, exposure

# Research & Development (R&D) 

Research and development remain a key pillar of JSL’s growth strategy, driving product innovation, operational excellence, and enduring value creation. The Company focuses on developing high-performance stainless steel solutions, strengthening metallurgical capabilities, and advancing sustainable manufacturing practices to meet evolving customer and industry requirements. JSL’s R&D efforts are also directed towards improving process efficiency, developing specialised grades, and supporting the transition towards environmentally responsible technologies. Through collaborations with academic institutions, research organisations, and industry partners, the Company continues to promote innovation and develop solutions that address emerging market needs. 

In FY26, JSL upgraded its product innovation capabilities by developing the stainless steel grade SM650 in thinner gauges, offering a yield strength of over 700 Megapascal (MPa) for applications such as coal tippers and ash containers. The Company also developed a stainless steel grade containing 5% silicon for sulphuric acid storage, expanding its product portfolio for the processing and industrial sectors. JSL also advanced its research and product development capabilities by successfully commercialising India’s first 9Cr1Mo plate for steam generator applications and supplying it to BHEL. Also, it developed and exported the martensitic grade 1.4110 for specialised knife applications, while engineering a high-nickel 304 grade with restricted ferrite content to meet Larsen & Toubro’s structural requirements, demonstrating its focus on innovation, import substitution, and high-performance stainless steel solutions. 



# Internal Financial Controls 

JSL maintains a robust internal financial control framework to ensure the accuracy, reliability and integrity of its financial reporting processes. Regular reviews and assessments conducted during the year confirmed that these controls were functioning effectively, with no material weaknesses identified. The Company’s strong control environment reflects its commitment to sound financial governance, transparency and responsible business practices. 

The Company continues to strengthen and refine its internal control systems to remain aligned with evolving regulatory requirements and industry best practices. In addition, JSL conducts regular training and awareness programmes to help employees better understand internal control procedures and compliance requirements. These initiatives support a culture of accountability, ethical conduct and strong governance across the organisation, while reinforcing the importance of compliance at every level.
